rationale: This is a pure operator swap (MIN for MUL) on the identical two legs of the archive's "Short-Debt Coverage Liquidity Value," i.e. exactly the kind of cosmetic variant of an existing signal that adds no new economic content since rank-product and rank-min are highly collinear.

The numerators are unchanged from the archived "Liquid Distribution Capacity" and the only edits are denominator swaps borrowed from two other already-tested signals (+dlc in the value leg, cogs+xsga in the quality leg), making it a recombination of known winning legs rather than a new mechanism; the stated rationale about avoiding zero-payer ties is also inapt since the original already pooled dvc with cash.

Separating near-term net liquidity (che−dlc) from total net cash while moving long-term debt into the valuation denominator is a genuinely different balance-sheet decomposition from the archived net-cash and short-debt-coverage signals, and the sign logic matches the expression, though the profitability leg is a standard workhorse so the incremental information is modest.

Substituting operating cash flow for SG&A in the liquid-resources numerator is an economically meaningful change of theme (self-funding vs. organizational platform) rather than a rescaling, but adding a stock (che) to an annual flow (oancf) is dimensionally crude and the result will likely be dominated by the well-known cash-flow-to-price effect.

The proposal is internally consistent and, unlike the other entries, is explicitly motivated by the diagnosed fmb/alpha divergence in the sales-yield family, but sales-to-price times gross/operating profitability is close to a textbook value-quality composite and the che/at buffer is a light addition to a leg that has already failed three times on alpha.

This is effectively a re-parameterization of the archived "Cash-Runway Glamour Burn" (same negated after-interest profitability leg, same cash-versus-short-debt-versus-market-value cheapness leg, just rearranged) and it also largely mirrors this batch's own Net Current Liquidity Surplus, so it tests little that is new.
